sentences.ko: 있잖아, 무슨 일이 있어도 우리는 네 편이고 널 사랑해.
sentences.text: Well, look, whatever happens, we're here for you and we love you.

alts.text: No matter what, we've got you. Love you.
Whatever may happen, we are here for you, and we love you.

sentences.note: **we're here for you** 는 힘든 일을 앞둔 사람에게 '우리가 곁에 있어' 하고 응원할 때 쓰는 말입니다. **whatever happens** 를 앞에 붙이면 '결과가 어떻게 되든' 이라는 뜻이 더해집니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 좋아, 그냥 하려던 말 해 버릴게.
sentences.text: Okay, I better just say what it is I'm going to say.

alts.text: Alright, I'm just gonna say it.
Very well, I had better simply say what I intend to say.

sentences.note: 꺼내기 어려운 말을 앞두고 마음먹을 때 **I better just say** 로 시작합니다. **what it is I'm going to say** 는 '하려던 그 말' 을 힘주어 가리키는 말투입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 언니가 지금 전화 기다리고 있거든. 주말에 자기 산장 써도 된대, 스키 타러 가자고.
sentences.text: Because I have my sister on hold and she said that we could have her cabin for the weekend and go skiing.

alts.text: My sister's waiting on the line — says we can use her cabin this weekend and ski.
My sister is waiting on the other line, and she has offered us her cabin for the weekend so that we can go skiing.

sentences.note: **on hold** 는 통화를 잠깐 대기시켜 둔 상태입니다. 남의 집이나 물건을 잠깐 빌려 쓸 때 **have her cabin for the weekend** 처럼 have 를 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 이렇게 쿠키를 많이 구운 건 중3 이후로 처음이야.
sentences.text: Well, I've not made this many cookies since I was in the ninth grade.

alts.text: Haven't baked this many cookies since ninth grade.
I have not made so many cookies since I was in the ninth grade.

sentences.note: '~ 이후로 처음이다' 를 영어로는 **not made this many cookies since** 처럼 '~ 이후로 이만큼 안 했다' 고 말합니다. 미국의 **ninth grade** 는 우리로 치면 중3입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 네 사이즈 알거든. 진짜 괜찮은 걸로 골라 올게.
sentences.text: I know your size and I'm going to I'm going to pick out some really good stuff for you.

alts.text: Got your size — I'll grab you some nice stuff.
Since I know your size, I will choose some very good things for you.

sentences.note: 옷이나 선물을 대신 사 줄 때 **I know your size** 하고 말을 꺼냅니다. 여러 개 중에서 골라 온다는 뜻은 choose 보다 **pick out** 이 훨씬 흔합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 아, 나도 정말 그러고 싶은데 오늘은 좀 피곤해서.
sentences.text: You know, I I'd love to, but I'm a little tired.

alts.text: Wish I could, but I'm kinda beat.
I would be glad to, but I am somewhat tired tonight.

sentences.note: **I'd love to, but** 는 누가 뭘 하자고 할 때 기분 상하지 않게 거절하는 첫마디예요. 피곤하다는 말은 **a little tired** 처럼 살짝 낮춰 말해야 부드럽고, 편한 사이에서는 **kinda beat** 라고도 해요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 좀 엉뚱하게 들리는 것도 있다는 건 나도 알아. 그래도 그렇게까지 말할 건 없잖아.
sentences.text: Look, I know that some of this stuff is out there, but I mean, come on.

alts.text: Yeah, some of it's kinda weird, but c'mon.
I understand that some of this is rather unusual, but please be fair.

sentences.note: **out there** 는 생각이나 얘기가 '너무 엉뚱하다, 괴짜 같다'는 뜻이에요. 끝의 **come on** 은 상대가 너무 몰아붙인다 싶을 때 '에이, 그건 좀 아니지' 하고 받아치는 말이에요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그러니까 될 확률이 높은 쪽에 걸어야지.
sentences.text: So So you got to play the odds.

alts.text: Gotta go with the odds.
Therefore, you must bet on whatever is most likely to happen.

sentences.note: **play the odds** 는 확실하지는 않아도 가능성이 높은 쪽을 고른다는 말이에요. 뭘 할지 고민하는 친구한테 '어차피 모르는 거니까 확률 높은 데 걸어' 할 때 써요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 회사에 어떤 여자분이 이걸 2주 내내 썼는데, 그 뒤로 담배를 한 번도 안 피웠대.
sentences.text: This woman at work used it for two weeks straight and she hasn't smoked since.

alts.text: A woman at my work used it two weeks straight, hasn't smoked since.
A colleague of mine used it for two consecutive weeks, and she has not smoked since then.

sentences.note: **two weeks straight** 는 '2주 동안 하루도 안 빼고'라는 뜻이에요. **hasn't smoked since** 처럼 since 하나만 끝에 붙이면 '그 뒤로 쭉'이 돼서, 뭔가를 권할 때 효과를 말하기 좋아요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.text: I'm just going to hang out as friends.

alts.text: We're just hanging out, as friends.
We are simply going to spend time together as friends.

sentences.note: **hang out** 은 특별한 목적 없이 같이 놀거나 시간을 보내는 거예요. 데이트냐고 물어볼 때 **as friends** 를 붙이면 '그런 거 아니고 친구로'라고 선을 긋는 말이 돼요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends
